sections.h2: What stands between an Orange owner and a closing
sections.html:
In the City of Orange Township, state law is not the only hurdle: the city code makes it unlawful to sell or transfer a residential property until a certificate of habitability is issued. Owner and buyer share responsibility for getting it, so plan for it at contract stage.

Orange covers 2.21 square miles in Essex County and has 35,642 residents in the July 2025 estimate, up from 34,447 at the 2020 census. That works out to more than 15,000 people per square mile. It borders East Orange, Glen Ridge, Montclair, South Orange and West Orange.

Only 25.5 percent of housing units are owner-occupied, the median owner-occupied value is $365,500 and the median gross rent is $1,550. With three in four housing units renter-occupied, expect some buyers to be small landlords rather than owner-occupants. Median household income is $52,847, so buyers tend to weigh repair costs closely when they set an offer.

Orange has housing from the railroad era onward, and the inspection fee rises with the number of units, so owners of two- to five-unit buildings should read the fee schedule first.

sections.h2: Applying for the certificate of habitability
sections.html:
Chapter 156, Article VII of the city code requires a certificate of habitability, issued by the Division of Code Enforcement, before any residential property is sold, purchased, conveyed or transferred. The application is filed at 29 North Day Street, Room 305, and it must include a fully executed sales contract. The steps on the city's application are:

  • Check with the Building Division whether the property has open building permits, because all permits must be closed before a permanent certificate issues.
  • Complete the transaction information and attach the sales contract or deed.
  • Pay by certified check or money order made out to the City of Orange Township.
  • If the buyer is a company, supply its organization documents and a photo ID for the responsible member.
  • Schedule the fire certificate inspection with the Orange Fire Department.

Condominiums and townhouses skip this form and apply for a Certificate of Occupancy through the Building Division instead.

The fee depends on the number of units.

Certificate of habitability fee by building size
Number of unitsFee
One$200

Four$500
Five$600
Six to nine$1,000

A second re-inspection costs $100 for a one-unit home. A missed appointment can trigger another inspection fee, so confirm access before the date. Payment is only by certified check or money order, and Code Enforcement can confirm the current figures before you write a check.

You can, with conditions. If the contract calls for an as-is conveyance, the contract goes with the application and both owner and purchaser must sign it. If the inspection finds violations that cannot be fixed before closing, Code Enforcement may issue a temporary certificate of habitability, which is nonrenewable and good for no more than six months from the conveyance or possession date.

For a vacant or run-down house, the city's application asks for a letter from the buyer's attorney, signed by the buyer, acknowledging that permits must be obtained before renovations and that the property must stay unoccupied until a permanent certificate is granted.

The code exempts four kinds of transfer:

  • Transfers between immediate family members, including spouses.
  • A property certified within the previous six months.
  • A property bought to be demolished, after written notice to Code Enforcement and a demolition permit application.
  • A transfer by probate to heirs or beneficiaries under a will.

Orange carries a heavy tax burden. In 2020 its equalized property tax rate was 4.679 percent, against a 2.279 percent statewide average, which put it 12th highest in New Jersey. Buyers will compare your carrying costs with other towns, so have recent bills ready.

The seller's Realty Transfer Fee is separate and comes from the state's rate schedule. The buyer's extra 1 percent fee starts above $1,000,000. Every deed needs a Gross Income Tax form too: the GIT/REP-3 for New Jersey residents, and GIT/REP-1 or GIT/REP-2 for nonresident sellers who must prepay. If you appeal an assessment, the Essex County board of taxation must receive the petition by April 1, or 45 days after notices are mailed if later.

Interstate 280 crosses the city from West Orange to East Orange, and Central Avenue is County Route 508. Valley Street, Lincoln Avenue, Scotland Road and Highland Avenue carry local traffic. The Orange and Highland Avenue stations on NJ Transit's Morris and Essex Lines reach Newark Broad Street, Secaucus Junction and New York Penn Station, and ten NJ Transit bus routes serve Newark and local trips. Name the nearest station in your listing, since commuters search by it.

sections.h2: A practical order for an Orange sale
sections.html:
Work from the contract outward. Once you have a signed contract, call Building about open permits and close them, since no permanent certificate issues until they are cleared. Then file the habitability application at Code Enforcement with the contract, a certified check or money order and any buyer entity papers, and book the fire certificate inspection with the Orange Fire Department.

If the inspection turns up violations that cannot be repaired by closing, ask about the temporary certificate before the closing date, because it needs the as-is contract and the buyer's attorney letter. Tell the closing attorney early which exemption, if any, you think applies, so the paperwork matches.

When you go to the office on North Day Street, bring the fully executed contract, the deed or transaction information, payment by certified check or money order and, if the buyer is a company, its organization documents and a photo ID for the responsible member. If the house is vacant or run-down, ask the buyer's attorney early for the signed letter about permits and occupancy, since the application asks for it and a missing letter stalls the file.

A cash buyer who accepts the house as it stands does not shorten the city's process, but does remove the lender's repair demands. The certificate is still required, and so is closing out permits. Agree in the contract who attends the inspection, who pays the fee and who pays for any re-inspection if a first visit fails.

faqs.q: Do I need a certificate of habitability to sell a house in Orange, NJ?
faqs.a: Yes. The city code makes it unlawful to sell or transfer residential property until the Division of Code Enforcement issues a certificate. Condominiums and townhouses use a Certificate of Occupancy application through the Building Division instead.

faqs.q: How much is the Orange certificate of habitability fee?
faqs.a: The application lists $200 for a one-unit property, $300 for two units, $400 for three, $500 for four and $600 for five. Pay by certified check or money order payable to the City of Orange Township, and confirm the current schedule with Code Enforcement.

faqs.q: Can a buyer take an Orange house with violations?
faqs.a: Sometimes. For an as-is sale, Code Enforcement may issue a temporary certificate of habitability valid for up to six months, and it cannot be renewed. The contract and a buyer's attorney letter go with the application.

faqs.q: Are any Orange transfers exempt from the certificate?
faqs.a: Yes. The code exempts transfers between immediate family members, properties certified in the previous six months, properties bought for demolition and probate transfers to heirs or beneficiaries under a will.

faqs.q: How does the high Orange tax rate affect a sale?
faqs.a: It affects what buyers will pay. The 2020 equalized rate was 4.679 percent, compared with 2.279 percent statewide. A seller who believes the assessment is too high can petition the Essex County board of taxation by April 1.
